questions.title: Planning an experiment — oscillations of a suspended bar

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: rod fixed horizontally to two retort stands (clamped to the stands, stands on a bench); bar suspended from the rod by two vertical strings so that the bar is horizontal; metre rule; stopwatch; top-pan balance. Label the rod, string, bar, a (equal horizontal distance of each string from the centre of the bar), L (separation between the rod and the bar) and the centre of the bar.
Procedure and measurements: vary a (independent variable) and measure the period T of the oscillations (dependent variable), keeping L constant; mark the centre of the bar (measure the length of the bar with a rule and divide by 2) and measure a from the centre to each string with a rule; displace one end of the bar horizontally and release it; measure the time t for n oscillations (n at least 5) with the stopwatch and calculate T = t/n; repeat for the same value of a and take the average; repeat for a range of at least six values of a.
Analysis: plot a graph of lg T against lg a; the relationship T = (2πP/a^q)·√(L/M) is valid if a straight line (not through the origin) is obtained; gradient = −q, so q = −gradient; y-intercept = lg(2πP√(L/M)), so P = √(M/L)·10^(y-intercept)/(2π). (Equivalently plot lg T against lg(1/a) — gradient = q — or lg a against lg(1/T) — gradient = 1/q.)
Controls: keep L constant (same string length) and M constant (same bar); keep the bar horizontal and the strings vertical (check with a spirit level or set square); use a small amplitude and a fiducial marker at the midpoint of the oscillation; prevent the strings from sliding (notches, grooves or adhesive putty); use a large value of L to increase T and reduce the percentage uncertainty in T.
Safety: G-clamp the stands to the bench, or place cushions/a sand tray on the bench below the bar, to prevent the bar or rod from falling onto the bench.

questions.title: Analysis of data — terminal velocity of a falling sphere

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
t = 18βz/(gd²(ρ − σ)) = [18βz/(g(ρ − σ))] × 1/d²
Comparing with y = mx: gradient = 18βz/(g(ρ − σ))

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
All six points from (b) plotted correctly — each within half a small square of its true position, with point diameter less than half a small square (check the second and fourth plots from the left; ecf from 2(b)).
Error bars in 1/d² plotted for all six points — total length of each bar accurate to less than half a small square and symmetrical about the point.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer:
Straight line of best fit drawn (not from the top point to the bottom point; line thickness less than half a small square; must pass between (0.064, 2.50) and (0.066, 2.50) and between (0.134, 5.50) and (0.138, 5.50)).
Worst acceptable line drawn — the steepest or shallowest line that passes through all the error bars (may be constrained by an intermediate error bar).
Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer:
Using two widely spaced points on the best-fit line (Δx at least 0.07), with clear substitution into Δy/Δx:
gradient = (5.50 − 2.50)/(0.134 − 0.064) = 3.00/0.070
= 43 s mm⁻² (expect about 36–48 s mm⁻², i.e. (3.6–4.8) × 10⁻⁵ s m²)
Absolute uncertainty = gradient(best fit) − gradient(worst acceptable line), or ½(steepest gradient − shallowest gradient)
gradient = 43 ± 2 s mm⁻², i.e. (4.3 ± 0.2) × 10⁻⁵ s m²

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.answer:
β = gradient × g(ρ − σ)/(18z) = 4.3 × 10⁻⁵ × 9.81 × 6600/(18 × 0.097) = 2.78/1.746
= 1.6 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ (expect about 1.5; 2–3 s.f.; ecf from 2(c)(iii) and 2(d))
Unit of β: kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ (or Pa s)

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.answer:
%unc(β) = (Δgradient/gradient + Δ(ρ − σ)/(ρ − σ) + Δz/z) × 100%
= (2/43 + 100/6600 + 2/97) × 100%
= (4.7% + 1.5% + 2.1%) = 8.3% (answer must be greater than 2%; max/min method allowed)
